summary: Eleven comment-endorsed tools, apps, games, and learning resources, filtered against the 90-day history.
telegram_footer: 11 items surfaced | 30/30 prior-day front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: apswutils
items.summary: An ergonomic Python SQLite API built on APSW, praised after sustained use.
items.why_included: The maintainer reports extensive successful use over one to two years.
items.evidence: The commenter ported sqlite-utils to APSW and reports that extensive use has worked great.

evidence_sources.author: jph00
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using it a lot over the last year or two and it's worked great.

items.name: MkDocs
items.source_story_title: I paid people to try and follow my README
items.summary: A Markdown documentation-site generator; one user praises GitHub-driven automatic publishing.
items.why_included: A concrete first-hand endorsement describes a working documentation publishing loop.
items.evidence: The commenter says MkDocs works well and uses a GitHub job to update documentation on main-branch commits.

evidence_sources.author: alaudet
evidence_sources.excerpt: I found mkdocs works pretty well and integrated with a github job that updates the docs when I commit changes to my main branch.

items.name: Nushell
items.source_story_title: The tilde in your PATH may not be your HOME
items.summary: A structured-data shell that pipes tables and records instead of fragile text.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly recommends shell alternatives and identifies Nushell's concrete benefit.
items.evidence: The commenter recommends better-designed shells and praises Nushell's structured pipelines for avoiding fragile text parsing.

evidence_sources.author: malux85
evidence_sources.excerpt: Nushell (https://www.nushell.sh/): Passes structured tables and records between commands : avoids fragile parsing of text with awk/grep.

items.name: Diffle
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Diffle, a keyboard-centric diff viewer with LSP support
items.summary: A keyboard-centric diff viewer with LSP support, attracting interest for code reviews.
items.why_included: An independent commenter explicitly praises the project as a potential review aid.
items.evidence: The commenter says Diffle looks great and may help the review bottleneck; this is interest, not a usage report.

evidence_sources.author: aktenlage
evidence_sources.excerpt: This looks great, I need to try it. Reviewing is such a bottleneck now and this may help.

items.name: VoiceInk
items.source_story_title: Show HN: BetterWispr – Free, open-source dictation for Mac
items.summary: An open-source Mac dictation app, praised for reliably transcribing consultation notes.
items.why_included: A targeted reply provides a stronger first-hand endorsement than the initial mention.
items.evidence: The commenter reports flawless dictation for three users, with some initial compilation time.

evidence_sources.author: abyssin
evidence_sources.excerpt: VoiceInk took a little time compiling but it's been working flawlessly for the three people that use it now for dictating consultation notes.

items.name: Shelter
items.summary: An Android work-profile app for isolating apps and their access to photos.
items.why_included: A first-hand user endorses its isolation benefits while acknowledging inconvenience.
items.evidence: The commenter uses Shelter for WhatsApp and values default photo isolation, while describing the workflow as more annoying.

evidence_sources.author: jurf
evidence_sources.excerpt: It’s a bit more annoying but also isolates stuff like photos etc. by default, so you don’t have to think about it.

items.name: WallHop
items.source_story_title: Show HN: WallHop – 12ft.io is gone, so I built a replacement
items.summary: A web paywall-bypass service, bookmarked by a commenter seeking less archive friction.
items.why_included: An independent commenter gives an explicit positive endorsement rather than a bare link.
items.evidence: The commenter immediately bookmarks WallHop and contrasts it favorably with the friction of archive.is.

evidence_sources.author: SmashDan
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is great, straight into my bookmarks. I've been using archive.is but it's much more of a faff.

items.name: Beyond All Reason
items.source_story_title: Total Annihilation, rebuilt for modern computers
items.summary: An open-source RTS praised for polished controls and enormous battles.
items.why_included: Fresh specific praise supports resurfacing after the previous report's cooldown expired.
items.evidence: The commenter calls BAR the best spiritual successor and praises its polish and quality-of-life features.

evidence_sources.author: modeless
evidence_sources.excerpt: There have been several of these, but I think BAR is by far the best. It's open source, but looks nice and is polished. It has amazing quality-of-life features I haven't seen in any other RTS.

items.name: Zero-K
items.source_story_title: Total Annihilation, rebuilt for modern computers
items.summary: An open-source Total Annihilation-inspired RTS, explicitly recommended for genre fans.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly prefers Zero-K and recommends trying both competing RTS games.
items.evidence: The commenter prefers Zero-K over Beyond All Reason and recommends genre fans try both.

evidence_sources.author: vladms
evidence_sources.excerpt: I do prefer Zero-K over Beyond All Reason, but I would recommend anyone interested in the genre to try both and decide for themselves.

items.name: Virtual Barbershop
items.source_story_title: How I reverse engineered a commercial spatial audio effect
items.summary: A binaural barbershop audio demonstration, fondly recommended in a spatial-audio discussion.
items.why_included: The commenter explicitly calls the concrete recording cool and supplies its video URL.
items.evidence: The commenter fondly endorses the Virtual Barbershop recording and describes its binaural microphones.

evidence_sources.author: andai
evidence_sources.excerpt: This also reminds me of this cool mp3 from the 2000s — maybe it's on YouTube these days — called virtual barbershop, which was recorded with binaural microphones.

items.name: Merchants of Doubt
items.source_story_title: Documents add to evidence in climate deception case against ExxonMobil
items.summary: A nonfiction book tracing organized doubt campaigns around tobacco and climate science.
items.why_included: An explicit book recommendation adds a grounded nonfiction discovery outside software.
items.evidence: The commenter says the book covers the topic well and calls it a fascinating read.

evidence_sources.author: abound
evidence_sources.excerpt: Since it doesn't look like anyone has mentioned it yet: the book "Merchants of Doubt" covers this topic quite well.
